headline.title: First flakes for Adirondacks.
headline.text: Up to {{s:2}} on the summit of Whiteface early Friday to Saturday morning. 27 of 31 resorts get cold enough nights for snow guns this week, mostly in White Mountains and Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Cool and quiet weather will continue through Thursday night.
A dynamic system will bring rain, gusty winds, and some higher elevation snow on the backside.
Temperatures trending above normal with mostly dry conditions prevailing Sunday through Tuesday of the extended forecast.

ALY.excerpt:
) After a rainy Friday, windy and colder weather is expected Friday night into Saturday. Gusts could down foliated trees and blow around unsecured outdoor objects. There is also the potential for snow showers in the ADKs Friday night into Saturday morning.
) Dry weather with seasonable temperatures are expected for the start of next week.

GYX.excerpt:
High pressure builds in tonight and Thursday for mostly dry weather.
Low pressure crosses Friday through Friday night bringing beneficial rainfall.
Seasonably cold and blustery conditions arrive for the weekend, along with the chance for a few downed branches. Wintry conditions hazardous to hikers are expected through the higher terrain.

BUF.excerpt:
) Widespread rain Thursday night through Friday.
) Much colder Friday night through Saturday night with a few wet snowflakes possible.

PHI.excerpt:
A cold front will sink south through the region this evening yielding cooler weather for Thursday.
A strong cold frontal passage Friday evening will bring windy conditions, showers and potential for some thunderstorms, and colder temperatures into the weekend.
Widespread frost and freeze conditions are increasingly likely Saturday night.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Friday morning to Saturday morning: Sugarbush {{s:1.4}}, Mad River Glen {{s:1.2}}, Smugglers' Notch {{s:0.6}} at the summits. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:28}} to {{t:55}}, with rain at times and gusts near {{w:42}} up top.
Snowmaking: Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough for snow guns this week (37). Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8.
NWS Burlington forecasters: "Cool and quiet weather will continue through Thursday night."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:0.5}} at the summit Friday morning to early Saturday (models {{r:0.3,4.2}}). It starts as rain ({{l:0.56}}), even at the summit, then changes to snow early Saturday as colder air arrives. It won't last: highs reach {{t:49}} Monday.
Snow guns can run early Saturday to Sunday morning: about 32 hours cold enough at the summit, getting down to {{t:18}} once humidity is factored in. The base is cold enough for 15 of those hours.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 43 days out. Openings depend on snowmaking nights, not the calendar.
